problem:
Which of the following has an ENTIRE integrand that is odd about zero and opposite integration limits, so the standard odd-function cancellation rule applies directly? This is an explicitly revised criterion question, distinct from asking which integrals have value zero. Independently solve and return an exact displayed option/value pair. Preserve in your explanation the distinction between the direct odd-integrand criterion and other ways of obtaining zero.

Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

- ${\int }_{-1}^{1}\sqrt[3]{x}\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x)\,\text{d}x$
- ${\int }_{-2}^{4}\frac{7{x}^{3}}{1+2{x}^{4}}\,\text{d}x$
